title: 选择 Interview Book 的视觉方向
question: 哪种视觉世界最适合长期承载中英文问题库？主卡会展示首页完整 comp；选中后我再做三版构图对比。

options.label: The Question Accession Register
options.lineage: Museum study-room accession registers and subject indexes
options.thesis: Every question is a clearly identified record, reachable through several independent subject indexes.
options.viewport: An operational index puts bilingual search beside topic headings, then shows one question record with its purpose directly attached.
options.case: The museum-register form makes stable IDs, subject headings, source attribution, and cross references feel like one coherent record.
options.risk: An archive can feel dusty or closed; live search and direct question links must remain prominent.

raised.raise: Grid discipline: use one explicit spacing grid and stable type hierarchy across index, record, and detail.
Emphasis budget: reserve one strong visual emphasis for search and the featured question.
Density control: align compact IDs and facets while keeping question prose comfortably readable.
Recoverable states: each question and filter remains a stable, directly linkable state.

options.label: The Editorial Interview Handbook
options.lineage: Well-edited professional reference books and interview columns
options.thesis: A readable editorial index makes the question and its purpose feel immediately useful.
options.viewport: A quiet masthead sits above direct search, topic navigation, and an editorially typeset featured question with a short purpose note.
options.case: The familiar professional reference is the easiest path into a large question collection and works equally for candidates and interviewers.
options.risk: It can collapse into a generic documentation template unless the question-purpose pairing owns the page.

options.label: The Film Editor’s Select Bench
options.lineage: Film cutting benches and perforated work-print select rails
options.thesis: Question discovery follows a physical select rail, with kept and deferred material still visible.
options.viewport: A select rail anchors the page; each frame is a question, and the open reader view reveals its purpose without turning into an answer.
options.case: The editorial curation metaphor is memorable and can help readers build a reusable question set, though selection is secondary today.
options.risk: It may overstate sequencing and imply that questions must be edited into one prescribed path.

options.label: The Provenance Ribbon
options.lineage: Museum object histories, custody records, and provenance exhibitions
options.thesis: A continuous source line connects each question to its context, adaptations, and related ideas.
options.viewport: A source-aware question index leads into one question record whose related topics and source history remain attached.
options.case: It makes attribution and adaptation legible, a useful discipline for an author-curated reference library.
options.risk: Provenance can dominate even though finding and understanding the question is the reader’s first job.

options.label: Bauhaus Foundation Workshop
options.lineage: Bauhaus foundation-course exercises in point, line, and plane
options.case: The exercise world is remote from interview preparation and makes the visitor arrange shapes instead of discover questions.
options.kept: A consistent alignment grid and explicit hierarchy, already raised into the accession register.

options.label: Street-Fair Flyer
options.lineage: Layered screenprinted street-fair posters and pinned handbills
options.case: Public flyers are recognizable, but collage and motion would compete with the question and its purpose.
options.kept: One strong emphasis for search and the featured question, without the collage or motion.

options.label: Data-Sublime Field
options.case: Its technical density is striking but hides the words and excludes nontechnical roles.
options.kept: Compact alignment for identifiers and facets while body copy stays readable.

options.label: Origami Sequence
options.case: A required step-by-step transformation would imply a prescribed journey and distract from open browsing.
options.kept: Questions and filters remain recoverable at stable, shareable URLs.

canonCard.label: The conventional docs site
canonCard.thesis: A standard documentation library with a top search, sidebar, and clean question pages.
canonCard.viewport: A familiar title, search field, topic links, and recent questions in a conventional documentation layout.
canonCard.risk: Easy to use but indistinguishable from many other docs sites.
